subject: Intermittent peak-hour surge: remediation request and proposed premium onramp
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <ops@cleverbank.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures and latency during peak window

Markus,

Over the last two business days (Aug 8-9) we've seen a recurring degradation during our 16:00–17:00 ET peak window across a subset of API calls to the Redwood hosted endpoints. Symptoms: 5–8% elevated request errors (5xx) and p95 latency rising by ~300–500ms for ~20 minutes before recovering. We've attached a short capture with sample request IDs and traces.

This is concerning because our renewal is coming up in September and our product team is evaluating whether we need stronger operational guarantees. We need two things: 1) immediate mitigation so we don't see repeated regressions this week, and 2) a proposal for how Redwood would prevent this class of peak-hour tail-latency events in future (commercial + technical).

We can share additional traces if useful. Tim Lang from our vendor ops is copied — he's assisting on the tracing and can share raw logs.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Director, Platform Ops
CleverBank
(ops@cleverbank.com)

Attachment stubs: Regional_Throughput_Report_Aug.pdf (summary), sample-traces.txt (IDs)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <ops@cleverbank.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures and latency during peak window

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the traces. I'm sorry you hit that during a critical window. I pulled the preliminary logs for the sample IDs you sent and see symptom patterns consistent with a short-lived routing pressure in us-east that caused a subset of requests to land on secondary nodes with cold KV caches — that explains the jump in p95 for a narrow time slice.

Immediate next steps we can take this afternoon:
- Enable a temporary capacity bump for your account in us-east (2x for the next 72 hours) to reduce chance of routing to secondary nodes.
- Turn on aggressive prefix caching for your most common endpoints to reduce cold-KV impact.
- Assign an SRE (Soojin) to run a quick post-mortem and share a remediation timeline.

I'll get the capacity bump scheduled once you confirm — it won't require any integration work on your side. We're also working a longer-term offering we think will directly address this class of peak-tail events; I've copied Grace to coordinate commercial terms and a pilot.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <ops@cleverbank.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures and latency during peak window

Elena — quick status and a proposed path forward (technical + commercial):

Technical readout (Soojin): preliminary analysis points at two contributing factors during the 16:00–17:00 ET surge window:
- Burst across many independent prefixes led to KV cache evictions on a fraction of warm nodes. That created a tail effect when requests were routed to those nodes while their KV caches warmed.
- The smart-routing policy routed overflow traffic to a secondary pool in the same region that had slightly different caching warmup behavior.

Mitigations we will roll out immediately:
1) Temporary capacity bump (2x) for 72 hours — scheduled within two hours of your approval.
2) Aggressive prefix/KV pre-warm for your high-volume endpoints (no code changes).
3) Short-term routing tweak to reduce overflow to secondary pool during your peak hour while we validate the other fixes.

Proposed premium onramp (to avoid recurring exposure):
- Pilot: \"Regional Reserved Premium\" — reserved capacity in us-east for your peak window (daily reservation for 16:00–17:30 ET), plus preferential routing to pre-warmed nodes.
- SLA uplift: target p99 <= 300ms for generation endpoints during reserved window; guaranteed availability at 99.95% for reserved capacity.
- Remediation: automatic crediting for p99 breaches (calculated per-day) and 24/7 priority SRE on-call during the pilot.
- Pilot duration: 3 months, after which we can bake the profile into your renewal.

I'm attaching a short regional report and a remediation playbook for your SREs. Grace will follow up on commercial terms — we can offer a pilot discount if we agree on a renewal commitment window.

Soojin, can you validate the operational steps and ETA to have pre-warm + routing tweak in place?

Elena — if that commercial shape looks workable I can send a formal SLA amendment and pilot statement of work.

Thanks,
Markus

Attachments: Regional_Throughput_Report_Aug.pdf, remediation-playbook.txt

From: Elena Martinez <ops@cleverbank.com>

Cc: Tim Lang <t.lang@finops.io>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 10:37:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures and latency during peak window

Markus / team — thanks for the quick analysis and the proposed mitigations. Tim and I reviewed the traces you requested, and Tim attached additional flow-level logs showing the exact request spikes and the request IDs you flagged.

We are open to a pilot but have two asks before we sign up:
1) Pilot pricing needs to include a program-level discount (we're evaluating multiple vendors for this renewal) — can you propose a commercial figure for the 3-month pilot?
2) We want an explicit clause: if we still observe materially elevated peak-hour tail latency after the pilot, we reserve the right to a 60-day exit and a partial license refund for the renewal term.

We also need a firm start date — our product freeze is Sep 6; we need the pilot active before that to influence our renewal decision.

Please include the SLO language and the proposed credit calculation in the amendment draft.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Director, Platform Ops
CleverBank

Elena — appreciate the clear asks. We've formalized the offer and attached the SLA amendment (SLA_Amendment_CleverBank_v3.pdf) plus the regional throughput report and a terse remediation playbook. Summary of the commercial / timeline items below: 

Commercial proposal (pilot):
- 3-month Regional Reserved Premium pilot in us-east (daily reservation 16:00–17:30 ET).
- Reserved capacity equivalent to 12 vGPUs (sized to match the observed surge).
- Pilot price: 25% discount off the standard Premium list for the pilot months (applied to reserved portion only).
- Renewal option: if CleverBank commits to a 12-month renewal within 30 days of pilot completion, we will hold pilot pricing for the first 6 months of the renewal.

SLA & credits (excerpt):
- Target p99 during reserved window: <= 300ms for generation endpoints; availability of reserved capacity 99.95% per month.
- Credit calculation: prorated daily credit equal to (reserved portion of monthly fee) * (breach minutes / total reserved minutes) with a minimum credit of one-day's reserved fee for any p99 breach day.
- Exit clause: If pilot fails to materially reduce peak-hour tail latency after 3 months and after two remediation cycles, CleverBank may exit with a 60-day notice and receive a pro-rated refund for remaining reserved fees applied to the renewal.

Operational commitments:
- Immediate: we scheduled the temporary 72-hour 2x capacity bump to begin within two hours of your approval (no integration required).
- Pre-warm + routing tweak: Soojin estimates 48–72 hours to deploy and validate.
- Priority SRE: 24/7 on-call during pilot window.

Next steps: 1) If you agree in principle, sign the attached SLA amendment via the DocuSign link and we will schedule the reserved capacity start date (we can target Aug 30 start). 2) Grace will follow up with a short purchase order template and final invoice terms.

Links and attachments: SLA_Amendment_CleverBank_v3.pdf, Regional_Throughput_Report_Aug.pdf, remediation-playbook.txt, DocuSign: https://docusign.example/sign/ABC123

If you want a call to review the amendment and credit math, Grace and I are available later this week.
